speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the appearance of the rash on your palms and how long it has been present? Additionally, have you noticed any similar symptoms on your soles or other parts of your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your occupation with livestock and rice farming, have you noticed any exposure to specific parasites or chemicals, and does the itching worsen at night? I also need to know if you have observed any scaling or depigmentation of the skin lesions.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on upper body and face. I also have Numbness and tingling sensation of both palms, Thinning of the eyebrows, Loss of some eyelashes, Hypopigmented macules around the elbows.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of hypopigmented macules, eyebrow/eyelash loss, and palmar paresthesia strongly suggests Hansen's disease. REQUEST TEST: Slit-skin smear for acid-fast bacilli.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the slit-skin smear was negative, could you describe the sensation in those hypopigmented macules on your elbows? I need to know if they are also numb or if you have lost the ability to feel touch, temperature, or pain in those specific spots.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as a farmer, no history of travel outside the local area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do the hypopigmented macules on your elbows lack sensation to touch, temperature, or pain? I also need to know if you have noticed any thickened peripheral nerves, particularly near your elbows or knees.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, changes in vision, or any respiratory symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The hypopigmented macules with eyebrow and eyelash loss are classic signs of leprosy, even with a negative smear which is common in paucibacillary disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Tuberculoid Leprosy
